title: CLI-centric SDK recipe pack: resumable streaming, idempotent retries, and edge adapters
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Goal: produce a compact, opinionated set of SDK examples and cookbook recipes that prioritize a CLI-first developer experience and robust streaming ergonomics. The pack will include: 1) a TypeScript Next.js example showing resumable streaming with SSE + reconnect tokens, 2) a Python FastAPI server example with Server-Sent Events (SSE) and safe restart semantics, 3) a Go HTTP server example focusing on graceful shutdown, streaming checkpointing, and KV-cache hints, and 4) a CLI example (Go + Python) that can resume interrupted streams using an idempotency+cursor pattern. The target audience is backend engineers and developer advocates who want copy-pasteable patterns that demonstrate retries, idempotency, resumability, and pragmatic batching/caching suggestions for low-latency interactive flows.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Next.js example (TS) demonstrates resume-on-reconnect with a short-lived resume token and shows tokenized partial output in the UI.
A2: FastAPI example exposes an SSE endpoint that emits structured chunks (tokens + partial parse) and supports client-provided idempotency keys for safe retries.
A3: Go HTTP server example includes graceful shutdown, context cancel propagation, and an example checkpoint file format to resume the KV cache/stream position.
A4: CLI examples (one in Go, one in Python) include a --resume flag, persist minimal cursor metadata, and survive network interruption in manual testing.

A5: Cookbook doc contains retry guidance: default backoff policy, when to mark idempotent, how to choose resume token TTLs, and examples for batching/caching recommendations with expected token-cost tradeoffs.
A6: All examples include short README usage instructions and a small test harness that simulates a mid-stream interruption and verifies resume behavior.
A7: Peer-reviewed by SDK and Docs (two engineers + one DevRel) and merged PR with CI examples passing.
technical_notes: Resumability model: server issues resume token after initial handshake; token encodes (model_variant, sequence_offset, ephemeral_kv_hash) signed with server key.
Idempotency: recommend idempotency-key header for non-streaming RPCs and idempotency+cursor combo for streaming. Use monotonic sequence offsets for validation.
Retries: default policy = exponential backoff jitter (base 200ms, max 8s, 4 retries) for transient errors; for 5xx or capacity errors use fallback to smaller model variant.
Streaming ergonomics: emit compact structured frames: {frame_type: token|partial_parse|meta, seq: int, data: string, checkpoint: optional}
Client parser: incremental JSONL-friendly single-token parse + finalization event to close partial parse state; clients should support idempotent append from a seq number to avoid duplication.
KV cache hinting: examples show how to provide prefix cache keys (e.g., conversation_id + prompt_hash) to suggest server-side cache hits; not required but useful for cost savings.
Security: resume tokens should be short lived (<= 60s) by default and scoped to a single model variant and route; longer TTLs allowed with stronger signing + audit logging.
Trade-offs: resumability increases complexity (token issuance, storage) but reduces user-visible latency for reconnects; doc explains operational cost and SLO implications.
Telemetry hooks: examples include lightweight counters for resume_attempts, resume_success, partials_emitted; map these to Console traces for later evaluation.
Interop: demonstrate patterns across TS/Python/Go SDKs so customers can adopt uniform semantics regardless of runtime.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Prototype minimal SSE-based resume flow in Next.js app (TS) with an in-memory resume token service (2d)
Step 2: Implement FastAPI SSE endpoint mirroring Next.js contract + small client helper in Python (2d)
Step 3: Build Go HTTP server example with graceful shutdown and file-backed cursor store + CLI that uses it (2d)
Step 4: Create Go and Python CLI examples that persist cursor metadata under ~/.redwood/recipes/ and accept --resume (1d)
Step 5: Write cookbook document explaining retry policy, idempotency guidance, TTL recommendations, and batching knobs (1d)
Step 6: Internal review (SDK + DevRel), iterate on ergonomics, add CI smoke tests that simulate interruption (1d)
Step 7: Merge, tag release sdks-2025.03, add links to Console recipes and docs (0.5d)
Note: total ~9.5 engineer-days; estimate split across two devs + review time.
